newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Russia push for more agribusiness investment.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Russia push for more agribusiness investment.

text.p: Several U.S. government agencies and officials in Russia hope to boost U.S. investment in Russian agribusiness by educating investors on opportunities that exist in Russia at the local level.

"By making a difference in the investment climate at the local level, you can attract U.S. investment," Christopher Goldthwait, general sales manager for the U.S. Foreign Agriculture Service said at talks held in Chicago on Tuesday.
Sponsored by the U.S. Agency for International Development, discussions were held to highlight investment opportunities in five targeted Russian oblasts, or local governments.
"We are focusing on five oblasts that are endowed with enormous natural resources," said John Lewis, director of Agriculture for USAID.
Some participants in the meeting said there were many successful Asian and European businesses operating Russia and warned that the U.S. could be left behind if early opportunities were not taken.
However, more help from the U.S. government--for example loan guarantees--will be needed to encourage the growth of private investment in Russia agribusiness ventures, one U.S. businessman said.
"Businessmen don't ask for a hand-out, but we'd like to have a level playing field," said Vladimir Gribovsky, owner of meat packing operations in Russia.
Agricultural topics addressed at the roundtable discussion included grains, oilseeds, fertilizer and other chemicals, farm machinery, beef, pork and poultry.

The next U.S./Russia agribusiness investment meetings are tentatively scheduled to be held in the targeted oblasts which are located in Western Siberia, Middle Volga and the Black Sea area. The agribusiness iniative is also sponsored by the Gore-Chernomyrdin Commission on Economic Cooperation.

U.S. companies that were registered to participate in Tuesday's talks included the pork producer Thorn Apple Valley, ferilizer producer IMC Global, Inc., poultry producer Tyson Foods, Inc. and farm equipment manufacturer Deere and Co..
